summary: Shows a module merging a util's spec via AnsibleModule::Create with an extra spec array, explains merge precedence (module wins, lists appended, dicts merged), and recommends a doc fragment documenting the shared options.
questions: How does a PowerShell module merge a util's argument spec with its own?
If the module and util define the same option, which wins?
How should I document options that come from a shared util?

answer_card.title: Use a shared util spec in a module
answer_card.answer_md:
```powershell
#AnsibleRequires -PowerShell ansible_collections.my_namespace.my_collection.plugins.module_utils.ServiceAuth
$module = [Ansible.Basic.AnsibleModule]::Create($args, $spec, @(Get-MyNamespaceMyCollectionServiceAuthSpec))
Invoke-MyServiceResource -Module $module -ResourceId $module.Params.resource_id -State $module.params.state
$module.ExitJson()
```
Module spec options take precedence; lists are appended; dicts get missing keys merged. Document shared options in a doc fragment and extend it in each module.
